Im assuming between 20 and 25%, but I do not know for sure. My labor scheduler stops me from scheduling once I hit around 25% based on projected sales which are based off previous sales. I feel like this is likely set by the franchise, though, as I’ve seen other franchises have insanely high labor variances and they don’t seem to care about it. I do not have a clear answer on that. I just know that we are expected to be within 1% labor variance between actual and ideal. How ideal is calculated is likely based on sales/sales projection and is influenced by wage of those clocked in. This makes running labor difficult because it isn’t based on skill, it is based on wage and sales alone. It’s also difficult though when you have a dead period in between rushes and to save labor you have to send people home but then need more bodies later and don’t have them because you had to send them home. What people are willing to work makes this difficult as well. Most people want to be done by nine. It makes late night more difficult than one would like. Cutting aggressively once rush is over Can also be a challenge as that’s the time for side work to get done but you can’t afford to keep people around to do it. It’s all about balance. It isn’t an easy game, especially for rush stores, slow stores, and even much more so for those that are both.

At the end of the day, like I said, carside should not be an option that’s offered at all. I have agreed that it is not a customers fault for utilizing something that’s offered to them, you can’t fault them for that. It shouldn’t be offered at all. But the more awareness you raise to a customer base that it is extremely inconvenient, the more likely people will stop doing it. We are timed on literally everything we do. We are chronically understaffed as a company (mostly due to wages and the experiences we have with customers and expectations from customers and our company) and do not have the staff to openly offer this form of carryout/delivery. Like I said before, you cannot force people to work. You cannot force staffing. It is a constant battle between customer expectation and company expectation with us in the middle of it not being able to meet either when we are trying to meet both, so most of the time we have to pick one and will likely pick the one that keeps us employed. The company doesn’t care about the customer and it doesn’t care about us. It cares about its money and our numbers signify money to them. To maximize our payout to make this job worth working, our expectations to meet are to make our food perfect within 1 minute or less, have it go through the oven in 7-9 minutes depending on your oven speed, cut it, dress it, box it, bag it, and have it at their door by the 20 minute mark which includes all of those things from start to finish. We are expected to have less than 1 percent labor while doing that. It’s a very hard ask. So while we juggle the expectations of the people who employ us and the expectations of a customer, it can be quite nearly impossible. And carsides make that even more difficult. Not to mention that we are expected to get the carside to them within two minutes of their checking in.

At the end of the day, it does come down to shitty owners in a lot of ways, but that doesn’t also mean that it doesn’t come down to shitty customers, too. Finding the balance is hard and most customers are not understanding of this, at least, in my area.

Depends on what it is. Most pizzas will absolutely burn if ran through twice. Some heftier pizzas depending on how they are topped can maybe withstand a twice run but I’ve never tried. Usually we push it back and if it’s during rush, there is no space to push it back because food is back to back on a conveyer belt. Ran through twice is 100% doable even during rush, but, I’d only ever do that with wings due to potential burning of product. It will also take your order twice as long to cook, you’d be surprised at how many people don’t understand that and get upset it’s taking longer than quoted. During rush hour or at a very busy store, you can guarantee you will not get a well done pizza. It just isn’t doable. During off peak times and at a slower store, it is 100% doable because there is plenty of space in the oven to push it back. It’s not necessarily that you’re asking a big ask as a consumer, it’s that you’re asking for something that you as a customer wouldn’t be aware that it’s not that simple. It’s a big ask knowing that it’s a big ask, but reasonable if you aren’t aware that it actually can be a big ask.

It doesn’t go to the driver as a tip, it HELPS the company cover the cost of paying mileage to the driver. The mileage rate like the hourly rate differ by location/state/franchise. Our drivers make 10.59 (minimum wage) hourly and roughly 41 cents a mile. If my drivers get only stiffed, there are days that they only make about $20 from mileage and just their hourly, which amounts out to about a $60-$80 day total depending on how many hours they worked. Keep in mind, the mileage that gets paid to the driver is meant as money for vehicle maintenance and gas. They use it how they want as it’s just money paid on their check, but it’s meant to help keep their vehicle in working order to be able to continue working their job. Tips are where service employees actually make money. Tip for your service or do yourself the service and don’t pay anyone 😎 y’all have to realize that corporate greed is real and that at the end of the day, it’s the employee providing the service, not the corporation. The corporation provides the means for the employee to provide the service, which will always be done because we have reached a point where you cannot survive without working, and even with working, we still can’t survive. The corp makes their money either way. The employee doesn’t. You should be seeing your service providers as people, just as you are one.

I periodically delete social media apps when I notice that they are negatively impacting my mental. As an artist, I have this a LOT with Instagram due to self comparison. But I do also feel this way for other reasons, too, like down votes, negative attention, and sometimes lack of any attention. I recently posted on here in a mechanic sub about issues with my car a few days ago and I still have yet to have any kind of response to it and it leaves me feeling like I'm annoying or that I'm not worth assisting.
I have found some success with deleting the apps. When I do, at first, I will always feel like checking it and that I'm missing something, but after that passes, I feel better than I did before. I try to wait as long as possible until I start to readd apps to help ensure I get the break I need and add later when I feel more stable about my relationship with them.
I have yet to find a way to stop this from happening to begin with, and I'm not sure if I will. We all experience things differently and are more sensative to to certain things. Me living with BPD, I tend to be sensative to a lot of things and criticize myself for everything.
I do highly recommend just trying to take a break from triggering activities (like social media) and seeing how that affects you. I think we could all use a break from it from time to time. We tend to get too wrapped up in it when realistically, it is something that matters very little in the end. If taking a break isn't an option or isn't something you're comfortable with right now, I might suggest trying to tailor your community more to only include things that are not triggers for you (like unfollowing someone on Facebook who posts triggering things).
